messages:
noah: Quick sync — FinSolve POC asks for a tight cost/latency tradeoff writeup. Two workloads: short Q&A (avg ~40 tokens/resp), and long-form summarization (avg ~1,200 tokens/resp). They want a recommended GPU footprint for a 3-week POC, an estimate of monthly token spend for the POC, and confirmation we can meet latency SLOs for short Q (p95 < 200ms). Also flagged a security questionnaire that must be answered before infra access. Any blockers?
maria: Timeline: 3 weeks, starts next Tues. Security questionnaire is standard — they need SOC2 scoping, network isolation for logs, and an IP allowlist. I asked for the questionnaire doc.
alex: Rough throughput assumptions? Need qps numbers to pick GPUs. Also clarify whether long summaries are streamed or single-shot. Streaming changes latency profile.
noah: Target is 50 rps for short Qs (concurrent mostly), and 5 rps for long summaries. Long can be single-shot (they don't need token streaming UI). Example daily traffic: 10k short Qs, 1k long summaries.
lee: For p95 <200ms on short Qs we should use a smaller context-optimized model variant + KV cache and batching at 4-8 requests. If peak concurrency hit 50rps sustained we'd recommend 2 x A10 (or 1 x H100) for the POC depending on model size.
olivia: Pricing note — hosted token rate estimate for this exercise: $0.00004 / token for generation (example calc only). Let's do a quick sketch:
```
short: 10,000 q/day * 40 tokens = 400,000 tokens/day
long: 1,000 q/day * 1,200 tokens = 1,200,000 tokens/day
total = 1,600,000 tokens/day => ~48M tokens/month
cost@0.00004 = 48,000,000 * 0.00004 = $1,920/month (generation only)
```
This leaves room in their $5k POC budget for infra/egress and a Dedicated small GPU pool if requested.
maria: Good. Also confirm we can do VPC peering for the security asks during POC? Customer wants temporary peering to pull sample data securely.
presales-bot: NOTE: security checklist item created — assigned to eng-security. Ticket #SEC-4921.
alex: Operational checklist: 1) model pin + fallback policy to smaller variant, 2) batching config (4), 3) prefix caching enabled, 4) canary deploy route. If we plan Dedicated for POC we need a 48-72hr lead time to provision GPUs in their region.
lee: If they insist on <200ms p95 for short Qs with an LLM that has 1,000M params, caching and quantized kernels help but you'd likely need a peak-optimized node (H100) to be safe. For a 7B-ish variant, 2xA10 with good batching should meet it.
olivia: From a pricing perspective, if they run at higher concurrency and more long summaries than forecast, tokens will be the primary driver. Recommend we present two scenarios: conservative (current ask) and stress (x2 long summaries). I'll prepare a slide with numbers.
maria: Action items: olivia to produce cost scenarios by EOD, alex/lee to confirm provisioning lead time and exact GPU recommendation, eng-security to respond to questionnaire in 48hrs. I'll send the questionnaire to presales and loop FinSolve.
noah: Perfect — thanks. If anyone sees a big mismatch in assumptions ping me. I’ll draft the success criteria for the POC: 1) Short Q p95 <200ms, 2) Long summary quality pass on 80% of prompt evals, 3) < $5k total POC spend.
